issue_snapshot.title: Follow-ups from #58: 4 from the review
issue_snapshot.body:
What the review and QA of PR #59 (for #58) found and did not fix there — filed as it merged, one ticket for the lot. ## From the review Non-blocking findings the reviewer approved despite: a statement about severity, not a judgement that they are wrong. ### The /activity loading fallback lost the screen-reader announcement and busy state that the deleted loading.tsx carried and that the sibling group skeletons keep. > The /activity loading fallback lost the screen-reader announcement and busy state that the deleted loading.tsx carried and that the sibling group skeletons keep. > > `app/activity/page.tsx:67` > > Evidence: Deleted app/activity/loading.tsx had aria-busy="true" on
and

Loading activity…

. The new fallback is plus ActivityFeedSkeleton, whose root is a plain
with neither. components/group-skeletons.tsx:43-46 (GroupPageSkeleton) keeps both, and docs ux says status changes are announced. git grep 'Loading activity' on the PR branch finds nothing. > > Fix: Wrap the fallback in
with

Loading activity…

, as GroupPageSkeleton does, and add a case to failed-feed.test.ts. ### On a failed feed the raw ?group= uuid is carried into the chips and Retry even when the groups read succeeded and the id is not one of the viewer's groups. > On a failed feed the raw ?group= uuid is carried into the chips and Retry even when the groups read succeeded and the id is not one of the viewer's groups. > > `app/activity/page.tsx:140` > > Evidence: ActivityContent line 140: groupId={scoped?.id ?? rawGroupScope(rawGroup)}. If listActivityGroups succeeds, scoped is null for a stranger's uuid, but rawGroupScope still returns it, so ActivityFailed puts that uuid in the hidden group input and the Retry href. The success branch drops it (scoped === null gives preserved={}). > > Fix: Use the raw fallback only when the groups read is what failed, for example track groupsFailed and write groupsFailed ? rawGroupScope(rawGroup) : (scoped?.id ?? null). Low impact: the scope is a filter, not an authorization, and the next successful load discards the id. ### Moving the "Showing X only" line out of the header changes its spacing on the loaded screen: it was gap-2 under the title row and is now a gap-5 sibling of the feed. > Moving the "Showing X only" line out of the header changes its spacing on the loaded screen: it was gap-2 under the title row and is now a gap-5 sibling of the feed. > > `app/activity/page.tsx:150` > > Evidence: Before:
held the title row and the scope line. After: the header is only the title row and ActivityContent's fragment is a child of
, so the scope line sits 20px below the title instead of 8px. The work order's AC list does not mention it and the skeleton fallback reserves an h-6 block that no longer matches the old rhythm. > > Fix: Keep the old 8px rhythm by wrapping the scope line and feed in a flex-col gap-2 / or give the scope line -mt-3; or accept it and say so in the PR description. ### The failed branch's comment says the raw id is carried only when the groups read failed, but the code carries it whenever the feed failed and the id is not a confirmed scope; the wire test pins the loose expression, so tightening it later breaks the test. > The failed branch's comment says the raw id is carried only when the groups read failed, but the code carries it whenever the feed failed and the id is not a confirmed scope; the wire test pins the loose expression, so tightening it later breaks the test. > > `app/activity/page.tsx:140` > > Evidence: page.tsx: `groupId={scoped?.id ?? rawGroupScope(rawGroup)}` under the comment 'When the groups read is what failed ... the raw id is carried'. guard-wire-status.test.ts third case is titled 'when the groups read is what failed' but only matches /groupId=\{scoped\?\.id \?\? rawGroupScope\(/. > > Fix: Track groupsFailed separately from rows failing and use it in the expression; update the regex and the comment together. --- **Check each one still reproduces before planning it.** They were written against the PR as it stood, and a later round can have fixed one. Some may not hold up: say so and drop them rather than implementing something that was never wrong. Split this if they turn out to be unrelated. Depends on #58.
